content.value_statement: Twitter/X data collection can require asynchronous queries, session setup, and careful rate-limit handling. This skill provides documented twscrape workflows for searches, profiles, timelines, and local result exports.
actual_capabilities: Install twscrape from PyPI or its public GitHub repository.
Configure API instances with local account databases and optional proxies.
Search public tweets with queries, filters, and result limits.
Retrieve public profiles, timelines, followers, following, replies, and retweeters.
Use asynchronous iteration and batch requests for documented collection workflows.
Export requested results to local text or JSON files.
limitations: Requires valid Twitter/X accounts, sessions, or cookies for many operations.
Twitter/X rate limits, suspensions, and platform changes can interrupt collection.
The skill does not guarantee compliance with Twitter/X terms, privacy law, or consent requirements.
It does not provide official Twitter/X API access or bypass authentication requirements.

use_cases.title: Monitor a public topic
use_cases.description: Search public posts for a defined topic and collect a limited result set for analysis.

use_cases.title: Review a public account
use_cases.description: Retrieve a public profile and recent timeline for a documented research task.

use_cases.title: Build an async collector
use_cases.description: Use asynchronous queries and local exports in a Python data collection workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic search
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me use twscrape to search public Twitter/X posts for "climate data" and return at most 20 results. Explain the required setup first.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve a public profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to retrieve a public Twitter/X profile by username with twscrape. Include safe handling for account credentials and cookies.

prompt_templates.title: Collect a limited timeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a twscrape workflow that collects up to 100 recent posts from a public account and saves the requested fields locally.

prompt_templates.title: Design a compliant collector
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an asynchronous twscrape collection plan for authorized research. Include limits, local database protections, logging, retries, and platform compliance checks.

output_examples.input: Search public posts for "python lang:en" with a limit of 20.
output: Setup checklist for an authenticated twscrape API instance.
Guidance for reviewing results and respecting platform limits.

output_examples.input: Collect a public account timeline and store it locally.
output: Steps to retrieve a public account identifier.
A local export plan with credential and database protection reminders.

best_practices: Use only accounts and data collection activities that you are authorized to access.
Store passwords, cookies, and local account databases outside source control with restrictive file permissions.
Set small limits, add delays, and follow Twitter/X terms, privacy obligations, and applicable law.
anti_patterns: Do not use account rotation or proxies to evade platform enforcement or collect data without authorization.
Do not hardcode real passwords, email credentials, or session cookies in scripts or prompts.
Do not collect, retain, or share personal data beyond the approved research purpose.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It documents twscrape workflows for collecting public Twitter/X data with Python.

faq.question: Do I need a Twitter/X account?
faq.answer: Many operations require valid accounts, sessions, or cookies managed by twscrape.

faq.question: Can I use this as the official Twitter/X API?
faq.answer: No. twscrape is a separate library and does not provide official API access.

faq.question: Where are account details stored?
faq.answer: The documented default is a local accounts.db file. Protect it with restrictive permissions and keep it out of source control.

faq.question: Can I use a proxy?
faq.answer: The skill documents optional proxy configuration. Use it only for legitimate network requirements and authorized activity.

faq.question: Does this guarantee compliance with Twitter/X rules?
faq.answer: No. You must review and follow current platform terms, privacy requirements, and applicable law.
